text:
Marcus Destin reflects on his journey and role at University of South Dakota
Marcus Destin found himself beginning a new chapter in Vermillion after unexpected changes to his university grants left him owing about $5,000, he recalled on July 8. "So there I was, in South Dakota with only what I had packed in my suitcase and no idea what to do next," Destin said.
Destin started working at a local chain restaurant while saving for his education. As he built relationships with University of South Dakota employees who visited the restaurant, he became more connected to the university community. Eventually, Destin enrolled in a bachelor’s degree program at USD and secured an internship that led to full-time employment.
Today, Destin serves as assistant director of student activities and multicultural affairs at USD. In this role, he helps students build community and find their paths within the university. "I get to watch students grow, gain confidence, discover more about themselves and eventually walk across that graduation stage with pride and purpose, ready to make an impact in the world," Destin said.
Destin is recognized for bringing energy to campus events as an emcee and game host for the South Dakota Coyotes. He has presented at national conferences, established traditions such as the Black History Month Game, and was named to USD’s 30 Under 30 list. These achievements are motivated by his desire to give back: "USD has given me opportunities that I honestly could not have imagined when I first arrived in Vermillion with just a suitcase and a lot of uncertainty about my future," Destin said.
He encourages alumni contributions beyond financial support: "You can give back through your energy, by showing up, supporting students... That’s how you build a culture. That’s how you build a true Coyote community." Reflecting on his time as both student and advisor for organizations like the Union of African American Students and Coyote Crazies brings him satisfaction as he watches new generations continue these groups’ growth.
The University of South Dakota offers several programs focused on student engagement across its departments. The Department of Sustainability and Environment promotes cultural well-being through action on campus or along the Missouri River; it uses facilities like the Akeley-Lawrence Science Center; functions within USD's College of Arts & Sciences; inspires positive change; is unique regionally for offering undergraduate/graduate degrees in sustainability; and extends its influence via partnerships such as with the Missouri River Institute, according to the official website.
